drs.label: DRS zones
drs.noZonesSeason: In {season} there is no zone or per-car overtake mode data
drs.noChannel: No data: this session does not include each car's DRS channel
drs.insufficient: No data: there are not enough DRS openings to infer the zones
drs.hintLabel: How the DRS zones are inferred
drs.hint: Inferred from where the cars had DRS open according to their telemetry, on laps on track and without neutralisation: they are not the official detection or activation lines, which no source provides. They start a little after the activation line (the driver's reaction) and end where drivers brake.
drs.hintCars: Inferred from the openings of {n} car. | Inferred from the openings of {n} cars.
drs.hintDiscarded: {n} car with an implausible DRS channel (open in more than half of its samples) is left out. | {n} cars with an implausible DRS channel (open in more than half of their samples) are left out.
drs.hintWindows: They look brighter while race control has DRS enabled and faint the rest of the time.
drs.hintNoWindows: Race control did not announce DRS in this session: the zones always look faint.
drs.hintZone: If race control disables a single zone, it only shows in its feed: without the zone geometry there is no way to tell which one it is.
drs.hintSeason: There is no DRS from 2026: active aerodynamics and overtake mode replace it, enabled track-wide by race control. The source gives neither the zone geometry nor a per-car channel.
drs.hintNoChannel: Without each car's DRS channel there is no way to know where it was opened, and no source gives the official zone geometry.
drs.hintInsufficient: A zone needs at least {passes} passes (one car on one lap) opening in the same place, from at least {cars} cars (or from the only one that opened it). In the wet or with few laps there may not be enough.
